info.bio:
Wendy Carlos (nacida como Walter Carlos el 14 de noviembre de 1939 en Pawtucket (Rhode Island, EE.UU.) es una compositora de música electrónica estadounidense. Carlos fue una de las primeras intérpretes famosas de música electrónica que usaron sintetizadores.

Su primer disco Switched-On Bach (Conectado con Bach, -en Latinoamérica-Bach electrónico o —en España— Enchufado a Bach) fue tal vez el primer álbum en intentar el empleo de sintetizadores como una alternativa a la orquesta.

podcast.title: A Clockwork Orange (1972) Score
podcast.body: Wendy Carlos, a classical musician who had been collaborating with Bob Moog on the development and application of his new modular synthesizers, was hired by director Stanley Kubrick to compose the score for his 1971 futuristic dystopian film, *A Clockwork Orange*. The entirely electronic score, released as a soundtrack in 1972 (with Carlos identifying as Walter Carlos at the time), introduced sounds no one had heard before and became a landmark in the widespread development of electronic music, influencing many rock musicians seeking novel sounds. "No one had ever heard such sounds. It was completely electronic."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: A Clockwork Orange Score (Early 1970s)
podcast.body: Walter Carlos composed the all-electronic score for Stanley Kubrick's movie *A Clockwork Orange*. The profits generated from these bold synthesizer experiments later funded a sex change operation. "after composing the all-electronic score for the Stanley Kubrick movie A Clockwork Orange."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Collaboration with Bob Moog
podcast.body: Carlos worked closely with Bob Moog at the Columbia-Princeton Electronic Music Center, where she offered a crucial musician's perspective on the design and feel of his new electronic instruments. Her input was instrumental in decisions like incorporating a keyboard and refining the tactile experience of individual keys, making synthesizers more user-friendly for musicians. "She worked carefully with Bob Mogue, offering a musician's perspective, and how his new electronic instruments should look and feel."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Collaboration with Bob Moog and Film Score Work
podcast.body: Wendy Carlos worked directly with synthesizer pioneer Bob Moog, using his innovative instruments. This collaboration led her to create the first all-synthesizer soundtrack for Stanley Kubrick's seminal futuristic film, *A Clockwork Orange*, demonstrating the significant artistic potential of the new technology. "That's from Wendy Carlos, who worked with Bob Mogue on his synthesizer. We created the All-Synth Soundtrack for Stanley Kubrick's futuristic Ecluckwork Orange."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Composing for "A Clockwork Orange"
podcast.body: In 1971, Stanley Kubrick hired Wendy Carlos to create the futuristic score for his movie "A Clockwork Orange." This opportunity arose after the commercial and artistic success of her album "Switched-On Bach," which showcased the synthesizer's capabilities for complex musical expression. "And when Stanley Kubrick was looking for a futuristic score for his 1971 movie, A Clock Recornch, he hired Wendy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Compositora de Bandas Sonoras de Cine
podcast.body: Wendy Carlos compuso las bandas sonoras para películas icónicas como "La Naranja Mecánica", "El Resplandor" y "Tron". Su trabajo en estas películas, realizado con su sintetizador Moog, la estableció como una figura clave en la aplicación de la música electrónica al cine. "Carlos hizo las mandas sonoras de la naranja mecánica, el resplando Oro Tron con su sintetizador MOOC."

srcs.episode: Ellas vieron el futuro: Pioneras de la música electrónica

podcast.title: Demonstration of Moog Synthesizer for BBC
podcast.body: Wendy Carlos provided a detailed demonstration of the Moog synthesizer for the BBC, explaining how sounds are built from fundamental waveforms. She illustrated the characteristics of sine, sawtooth, triangular, pulse, and square waves, emphasizing that sounds must be constructed rather than selected from presets. "To start to build these sounds, you have to start with something pretty simple."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dificultad de Aceptación de la Música Electrónica (Principios de los 60)
podcast.body: En una entrevista, Wendy Carlos señaló que a principios de los años 60 era extremadamente difícil que la gente escuchara y se tomara en serio cualquier tipo de música producida electrónicamente. En ese período, el público la consideraba "vanguardista en el peor sentido de la palabra" y sin ningún interés comercial, similar a la música cacofónica o concreta que ignoraba la melodía y la armonía. "En una entrevista índico que a principios de los 60 era muy difícil que la gente escucha si se tomas en serio cualquier tipo de música producida de forma electrónica."

srcs.episode: Ellas vieron el futuro: Pioneras de la música electrónica

podcast.title: Early Life and Academic Background
podcast.body: Originally known as Walter, Wendy Carlos pursued a dual major in physics and music at Brown University, later earning a master's degree in music composition from Columbia University in New York. Her academic foundation provided a unique blend of scientific and artistic understanding, which she applied to her musical innovations. "Wendy Carlos, originally known as Walter, was a physics and music major in Brown University, and later at Columbia University in New York, where she got a master's degree in music composition."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Identity Transition and Financial Independence
podcast.body: Originally known as Walter Carlos, she later transitioned to Wendy. The money earned from her work on "A Clockwork Orange" soundtrack played a role in this personal journey. "She was Walter then, Wendy now. It took the money he made from the Clock of Orange soundtrack. Which is on a way, came back as Wendy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Moog Gear Classical Recordings (Late 1960s)
podcast.body: A classical musician, Wendy Carlos, utilized Moog synthesizer equipment to record music, showcasing the new technology's potential beyond novelty. "Towards the end of the 1960s, a classical musician named Wendy Carlos used some Mogue gear to record music like this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Golden Age of Synths as told by OMD

podcast.title: Percepción de "Maldita Comercialemente" la Música Electrónica
podcast.body: Debido a la dificultad de aceptación y la percepción del público de la música electrónica como una vanguardia sin interés comercial, Wendy Carlos afirmó que la música electrónica estaba "maldita comercialmente hablando". Esta visión reflejaba el desafío que enfrentaban los pioneros en un género musical que rompía con las convenciones tradicionales. "Eso hizo afirma que la música electrónica estuve ese maldito comercialmente hablando."

srcs.episode: Ellas vieron el futuro: Pioneras de la música electrónica

podcast.title: Pioneering Synth for Sound Effects and Jingles
podcast.body: By 1966, Wendy Carlos was already utilizing an early Moog synthesizer to create sound effects and jingles for radio and television. This demonstrated the practical commercial applications of the new technology before its widespread adoption in classical and popular music. "By 1966, she was using an early Mogue synth to create sound effects in Jingles for radio and TV."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pionera del Sintetizador Moog
podcast.body: Wendy Carlos fue una de las primeras artistas en adoptar y explorar activamente el potencial creativo del sintetizador Moog. Su uso innovador ayudó a establecer este instrumento como una herramienta legítima en la música de vanguardia y el pop, desafiando las percepciones iniciales sobre la música electrónica. "Buen� hizo una de las primeras en adoptar y explorar el potencial creativo del sintetizador MOOC, ayudando a establecerlo como una herramienta lígitima en la música de Vanguard e IPUB."

podcast.title: Sex Change and New Identity
podcast.body: After achieving success with pioneering electronic music and film scores, Walter Carlos underwent a sex change operation, funded by the profits from these ventures. Wendy Carlos now lives and works in New York City. "The profits from those bold synthesizer experiments paid for a sex change operation, and now Wendy Carlos lives and works in New York City."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
